board_events.text: Many unbounded regions still give a perfectly good minimum — every cost-diet problem does.
'Region unbounded' describes geometry; 'solution unbounded' describes the answer. Never confuse them.
A maximum fails only when the region is unbounded in the direction $Z$ increases.
If the region is bounded, Theorem 2 guarantees both a max and a min — no special case can arise.

segments.text: Before the worked cases, burn one distinction into memory, because it is the single most common confusion in this chapter.
An unbounded region means the shape of the feasible set stretches off to infinity. That is a statement about geometry, about the picture.
An unbounded solution means the objective function has no finite optimum. That is a statement about the answer, about the value of Z.

The board makes the gap obvious. Here is one unbounded region. It clearly has a genuine minimum at the marked corner, yet the objective grows without limit in the up-right direction, so it has no maximum.
This is the everyday situation, not an exception. Many unbounded regions still yield a perfectly good minimum. Every cost-minimisation diet problem you formulated in Subtopic two is exactly this.
So keep the words separate. Region unbounded describes the geometry. Solution unbounded describes the answer. A region can be unbounded and still hand you a finite minimum.
When does a maximum actually fail? Only when the region is unbounded in the very direction that Z increases. If it opens the other way, the maximum can still exist.
And the clean guarantee. If the region is bounded, Theorem two promises both a maximum and a minimum, each at a corner. No special case can arise in a bounded region at all.
worked cases से पहले, एक distinction दिमाग़ में पक्का कर लीजिए, क्योंकि यही इस chapter की सबसे common confusion है।
unbounded region का मतलब feasible set की shape infinity तक फैलती है। यह geometry के बारे में बयान है, picture के बारे में।
unbounded solution का मतलब objective function का कोई finite optimum नहीं है। यह answer के बारे में बयान है, Z की value के बारे में।
board फ़र्क़ साफ़ कर देता है। यह रहा एक unbounded region। इसका marked corner पर एक असली minimum है, फिर भी objective up-right direction में बिना limit बढ़ता है, तो इसका कोई maximum नहीं।
यह रोज़मर्रा की situation है, कोई exception नहीं। कई unbounded regions फिर भी एक perfectly good minimum देते हैं। Subtopic two में आपने जो हर cost-minimisation diet problem बनाई, वो ठीक यही है।
तो शब्दों को अलग रखिए। region unbounded geometry बताता है। solution unbounded answer बताता है। एक region unbounded हो सकता है और फिर भी आपको finite minimum दे सकता है।
maximum असल में कब fail होता है? सिर्फ़ तब जब region ठीक उसी direction में unbounded हो जिसमें Z बढ़ता है। अगर वो दूसरी तरफ़ खुलता है, तो maximum फिर भी exist कर सकता है।
और साफ़ guarantee। अगर region bounded है, तो Theorem two maximum और minimum दोनों का वादा करता है, हर एक किसी corner पर। bounded region में कोई special case पैदा हो ही नहीं सकता।

sections.title: The tell-tale graph sign of each outcome

board_events.text: Each outcome and its tell-tale sign on the graph
Unique optimum: the objective line touches the region last at a single corner.
Multiple optima: two corners tie; the objective line is parallel to the edge joining them.
Unbounded solution: the region is unbounded and 'better than every corner' still overlaps it.
No feasible solution: the constraints share no common shaded region — the region is empty.
Redundant constraint: a line you can remove without changing the region at all.
Its line lies entirely outside, or along the far edge of, the region formed by the others.
Read the picture well and you can name the outcome before computing a single value.

segments.text: Each of the four outcomes leaves a distinct fingerprint on the graph. Learn the fingerprints and you diagnose the problem at a glance.
For a unique optimum, the objective line, as it slides outward, touches the region for the last time at a single corner. One clean winner.
For multiple optima, two corners tie for the best value, and the tell-tale sign is that the objective line runs exactly parallel to the edge joining those two corners.
For an unbounded solution, the region is unbounded, and the open half-plane meaning better than every corner still overlaps the region. There is always a feasible point that beats your best vertex.
For no feasible solution, the constraints share no common shaded region at all. When you shade everything, nothing is left over. The feasible region is empty.
There is also a fifth thing worth naming, a redundant constraint. This is a line you could remove entirely without changing the region.
You spot it because its line lies completely outside the region, or lies along the far edge, never actually forming a boundary that the other constraints have not already set.
The payoff is speed. Read the picture carefully and you can name the outcome, unique, multiple, unbounded, or infeasible, before you compute a single value of Z.
चारों outcomes में से हर एक graph पर एक अलग fingerprint छोड़ता है। fingerprints सीख लीजिए और आप एक नज़र में problem diagnose कर लेंगे।
unique optimum के लिए, objective line, बाहर slide करते हुए, आख़िरी बार region को एक अकेले corner पर छूती है। एक साफ़ winner।
multiple optima के लिए, दो corners best value के लिए tie करते हैं, और tell-tale sign यह है कि objective line ठीक उन दोनों corners को जोड़ने वाले edge के parallel चलती है।

unbounded solution के लिए, region unbounded होता है, और open half-plane यानी हर corner से better वाला हिस्सा फिर भी region से overlap करता है। हमेशा कोई feasible point होता है जो आपके best vertex को beat करता है।
no feasible solution के लिए, constraints का कोई common shaded region होता ही नहीं। जब आप सब shade करते हैं, तो कुछ बचता नहीं। feasible region खाली है।
एक पाँचवीं चीज़ भी नाम देने लायक है, redundant constraint। यह एक ऐसी line है जिसे आप पूरी तरह हटा सकते हैं बिना region बदले।
आप इसे पहचानते हैं क्योंकि इसकी line region के पूरी तरह बाहर होती है, या दूर वाले edge के साथ होती है, कभी असल में कोई boundary नहीं बनाती जो बाकी constraints ने पहले ना बना दी हो।
फ़ायदा है speed। picture ध्यान से पढ़िए और आप outcome को नाम दे सकते हैं, unique, multiple, unbounded, या infeasible, Z की एक भी value calculate करने से पहले।

sections.title: Precise properties: optima, unboundedness, infeasibility, redundancy

board_events.text: The properties, stated precisely
Multiple optima: if $Z$ is optimal at two corners, it is optimal at every point on the joining segment.

board_events.latex: Z(\text{corner}_1) = Z(\text{corner}_2) \;\Rightarrow\; \text{the whole joining edge is optimal}

board_events.text: Unbounded max test: for the largest corner value $M$, the maximum fails if $ax + by \gt M$ meets the region.
Infeasibility: if the intersection of all constraint half-planes (with $x, y \ge 0$) is empty, there is no solution.
Redundancy: removing a redundant constraint leaves the region — and the optimum — unchanged.
A bounded region can NEVER be infeasible or unbounded — Theorem 2 rules both out.
So the first thing to settle is always: does a common region exist, and is it bounded?

segments.text: Now the same four ideas stated as precise properties, the kind an examiner wants written down.
First, multiple optima. If Z attains its optimum at two corner points, then it attains that same value at every point on the segment joining them, giving infinitely many optimal solutions.
In symbols, when Z at corner one equals Z at corner two, the whole edge joining them is optimal.

Second, the unbounded maximum test. For a maximisation problem on an unbounded region with largest corner value big M, the maximum fails to exist if the open half-plane a x plus b y greater than big M has any point in common with the region.

Third, infeasibility. If the intersection of all the constraint half-planes, including x and y greater than or equal to zero, is the empty set, then the L P P has no feasible solution, and hence no optimal solution.
Fourth, redundancy. Removing a redundant constraint leaves the feasible region, and therefore the optimal solution, completely unchanged.
And the master fact that governs all of them. A bounded region can never be infeasible and never be unbounded. Theorem two rules out both special cases at once.
Which is why the very first thing to settle in any special-case question is this. Does a common region even exist, and if it does, is it bounded?
अब वही चार ideas precise properties के तौर पर, जैसा examiner लिखा हुआ चाहता है।
पहली, multiple optima। अगर Z अपना optimum दो corner points पर पाता है, तो वो वही value उन्हें जोड़ने वाले segment के हर point पर पाता है, जिससे infinitely many optimal solutions मिलते हैं।
symbols में, जब Z at corner one equals Z at corner two, तो उन्हें जोड़ने वाला पूरा edge optimal है।

दूसरी, unbounded maximum test। unbounded region पर maximisation problem के लिए, जिसकी largest corner value big M है, maximum fail हो जाता है अगर open half-plane a x plus b y greater than big M का region से कोई common point हो।

तीसरी, infeasibility। अगर सारी constraint half-planes का intersection, x और y greater than or equal to zero समेत, empty set है, तो L P P का कोई feasible solution नहीं, और इसलिए कोई optimal solution नहीं।
चौथी, redundancy। एक redundant constraint हटाने से feasible region, और इसलिए optimal solution, बिल्कुल unchanged रहता है।
और वो master fact जो इन सबको चलाता है। एक bounded region कभी infeasible नहीं हो सकता और कभी unbounded नहीं। Theorem two दोनों special cases को एक साथ ख़ारिज कर देता है।
इसीलिए किसी भी special-case सवाल में सबसे पहले यही तय करना है। क्या common region exist भी करता है, और अगर करता है, तो क्या वो bounded है?

sections.title: Detection procedures and a five-second triage

board_events.text: Detection procedures — spotting each case while solving
No feasible solution: plot all constraints; if no region is common to all, stop — 'no feasible solution'.
Unbounded solution: confirm the region is unbounded, find largest corner $M$, then test $ax + by \gt M$.
If that half-plane meets the region, write '$Z$ has no maximum' — but a minimum may still exist.
Multiple optima: evaluate $Z$ at all corners; if two tie, the whole joining segment is optimal.
Redundant constraint: if removing a line leaves the region unchanged, that constraint is redundant.
Run this as a triage BEFORE grinding through corners — it saves time and prevents classic errors.
5-second triage: common region? (else infeasible) → bounded? (if yes, both exist) → else verify.

segments.text: Here is how you actively detect each case while you are solving, rather than being surprised by it at the end.

To detect no feasible solution, plot and shade every constraint as usual, then look for a region common to all of them in the first quadrant. If no such common region exists, stop and write, the L P P has no feasible solution.

To detect an unbounded solution, first confirm the region is unbounded, then evaluate Z at all corner points and call the largest value big M, and finally test the open half-plane a x plus b y greater than big M.

If that half-plane shares any point with the region, then the objective can exceed big M, so you write, Z has no maximum. But remember, the same region may still have a perfectly valid minimum, so check that separately.
To detect multiple optima, evaluate Z at all corners, and if the optimum value is attained at two of them, then every point on the segment between them is also optimal.
To detect a redundant constraint, draw the region using all constraints, and if removing one line leaves the region unchanged because that line never forms a boundary, that constraint is redundant.
The smart move is to run all of this as a quick triage before you grind through the corner-point table. It saves time and prevents the classic special-case slips.

The triage is only five seconds. Is there a common region? If not, infeasible. Is it bounded? If yes, both a max and a min exist and there is no special case. Only if it is unbounded do you need the verification test.
यह रहा तरीका कि solve करते समय आप हर case को actively कैसे detect करें, आख़िर में चौंकने के बजाय।

no feasible solution detect करने के लिए, हमेशा की तरह हर constraint plot और shade कीजिए, फिर first quadrant में सबके common region ढूँढिए। अगर ऐसा कोई common region नहीं है, तो रुकिए और लिखिए, L P P का कोई feasible solution नहीं।

unbounded solution detect करने के लिए, पहले confirm कीजिए कि region unbounded है, फिर Z को सारे corner points पर evaluate कीजिए और सबसे बड़ी value को big M कहिए, और आख़िर में open half-plane a x plus b y greater than big M test कीजिए।

अगर वो half-plane region से कोई point share करता है, तो objective big M से आगे जा सकता है, तो आप लिखते हैं, Z का कोई maximum नहीं। पर याद रखिए, उसी region का एक perfectly valid minimum हो सकता है, तो उसे अलग से check कीजिए।
multiple optima detect करने के लिए, Z को सारे corners पर evaluate कीजिए, और अगर optimum value उनमें से दो पर मिलती है, तो उनके बीच के segment का हर point भी optimal है।
redundant constraint detect करने के लिए, सारी constraints से region बनाइए, और अगर एक line हटाने से region unchanged रहता है क्योंकि वो line कभी boundary बनाती ही नहीं, तो वो constraint redundant है।
समझदारी यह है कि यह सब एक quick triage की तरह चलाइए, corner-point table पीसने से पहले। यह time बचाता है और classic special-case slips रोकता है।

triage सिर्फ़ पाँच second का है। क्या common region है? अगर नहीं, तो infeasible। क्या bounded है? अगर हाँ, तो max और min दोनों exist करते हैं और कोई special case नहीं। सिर्फ़ अगर unbounded है, तब verification test चाहिए।

board_events.text: No pair satisfies $x + y \ge 12$ and $x + y \le 10$ at once — the shaded regions never meet.
The feasible region is empty, so there is no feasible solution and no optimal value of $Z$.

segments.text: Let us see infeasibility on a concrete problem. A coaching centre wants to run x morning batches and y evening batches, and it hopes to maximise total enrolment, Z equals thirty x plus twenty five y.
The staffing promise says it must run at least six morning and at least six evening batches. The room capacity says it can run at most ten batches in total per day.
So the constraints are x greater than or equal to six, y greater than or equal to six, and x plus y less than or equal to ten, with both variables non-negative.
Now look at the tension. The first two constraints together force x plus y to be at least six plus six, that is at least twelve.
But the room constraint demands x plus y at most ten. So we need x plus y to be both at least twelve and at most ten, which is impossible.
The board shows it geometrically. The block where x and y are each at least six sits in the upper right, and the triangle where x plus y is at most ten sits in the lower left. They never touch.
So no pair x, y can satisfy both x plus y at least twelve and x plus y at most ten at the same time. The shaded regions simply do not overlap.

Therefore the feasible region is empty. The L P P has no feasible solution, and there is no optimal value of Z. The interpretation is that the staffing promise and the room capacity are in conflict, and one of them must be relaxed.
infeasibility को एक ठोस problem पर देखते हैं। एक coaching centre x morning batches और y evening batches चलाना चाहता है, और वो total enrolment maximise करना चाहता है, Z equals तीस x plus पच्चीस y।
staffing का वादा कहता है कि उसे कम से कम छह morning और कम से कम छह evening batches चलाने ही हैं। room capacity कहती है कि वो रोज़ ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा दस batches कुल चला सकता है।
तो constraints हैं x greater than or equal to six, y greater than or equal to six, और x plus y less than or equal to ten, दोनों variables non-negative के साथ।
अब tension देखिए। पहली दो constraints मिलकर x plus y को कम से कम छह plus छह, यानी कम से कम बारह होने पर मजबूर करती हैं।
लेकिन room constraint x plus y को ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा दस माँगती है। तो हमें x plus y दोनों चाहिए, कम से कम बारह और ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा दस, जो impossible है।
board इसे geometrically दिखाता है। वो block जहाँ x और y दोनों कम से कम छह हैं ऊपर-दाएँ बैठता है, और वो triangle जहाँ x plus y ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा दस है नीचे-बाएँ। ये कभी नहीं छूते।
तो कोई pair x, y एक साथ x plus y at least twelve और x plus y at most ten को satisfy नहीं कर सकता। shaded regions बस overlap करते ही नहीं।

इसलिए feasible region खाली है। L P P का कोई feasible solution नहीं, और Z की कोई optimal value नहीं। मतलब यह कि staffing का वादा और room capacity आपस में टकरा रहे हैं, और इनमें से एक को ढीला करना होगा।

board_events.text: Test $5x + 4y \gt 40$: point (20, 0) is feasible and gives $Z = 100 \gt 40$. So NO maximum.
Push further — (100, 0) gives 500 — the value climbs without any limit.
Yet this region has a minimum: $Z = 32$ at (0, 8), since $5x + 4y \lt 32$ misses the region.

segments.text: Now the textbook trap, an unbounded region with no maximum but a perfectly good minimum. We maximise Z equals five x plus four y, subject to x plus y greater than or equal to eight, with both variables non-negative.
The problem is stated compactly, but read the constraints carefully.
There are only greater-than-or-equal and non-negativity constraints, so the region lies above the line x plus y equals eight and stretches away to infinity up and to the right. It is unbounded.
Find the boundary corners. At eight comma zero, Z is forty. At zero comma eight, Z is thirty two. So the largest corner value, big M, is forty.
A hurried student would stop and write forty. But the region is unbounded, so we must test whether we can beat it, and the board shows the answer visually.

Test the half-plane five x plus four y greater than forty. Take the feasible point twenty comma zero, since twenty is at least eight. There Z equals one hundred, which is greater than forty. A feasible point beats the best corner, so there is no maximum.
And we can push as far as we like. At one hundred comma zero, Z equals five hundred, and it keeps climbing without any limit at all.

But do not over-correct. This very same region does have a minimum. Z equals thirty two at zero comma eight, and this is verified because five x plus four y less than thirty two misses the region entirely. Unbounded region, no maximum, but a genuine minimum.

अब textbook trap, एक unbounded region जिसमें कोई maximum नहीं पर एक perfectly good minimum है। हम maximise करते हैं Z equals पाँच x plus चार y, subject to x plus y greater than or equal to eight, दोनों variables non-negative के साथ।
problem छोटे में दी है, पर constraints ध्यान से पढ़िए।
सिर्फ़ greater-than-or-equal और non-negativity constraints हैं, तो region line x plus y equals eight के ऊपर है और ऊपर-दाएँ infinity तक फैलता है। यह unbounded है।
boundary corners ढूँढिए। eight comma zero पर Z है forty। zero comma eight पर Z है thirty two। तो सबसे बड़ी corner value, big M, है forty।
जल्दबाज़ student रुककर forty लिख देता। पर region unbounded है, तो हमें test करना होगा कि क्या हम इसे beat कर सकते हैं, और board answer visually दिखाता है।

half-plane five x plus four y greater than forty test कीजिए। feasible point twenty comma zero लीजिए, क्योंकि twenty कम से कम eight है। वहाँ Z equals one hundred, जो forty से बड़ा है। एक feasible point best corner को beat करता है, तो कोई maximum नहीं।
और हम जितना चाहें आगे push कर सकते हैं। one hundred comma zero पर Z equals five hundred, और यह बिना किसी limit के चढ़ता ही रहता है।

पर over-correct मत कीजिए। इसी region का एक minimum ज़रूर है। Z equals thirty two, zero comma eight पर, और यह verified है क्योंकि five x plus four y less than thirty two region को पूरी तरह miss करता है। unbounded region, कोई maximum नहीं, पर एक असली minimum।

List the corners. They are zero comma zero, four comma zero, four comma two, two comma four, and zero comma four.

Removing it leaves the region — and the optimum of any linear objective — completely unchanged.

segments.text: The last special case is the redundant constraint. A feasible region is defined by x plus y less than or equal to ten, x less than or equal to twelve, and both variables non-negative. Which constraint is redundant?
Focus on the two upper limits and reason about them together in the first quadrant.
Within the first quadrant, the constraint x plus y less than or equal to ten already forces x to be at most ten, because y cannot be negative.

So the constraint x less than or equal to twelve can never actually bind. Every point that the other constraints allow automatically satisfies x less than or equal to twelve, since x is already at most ten.
The board makes it visible. The line x equals twelve sits well to the right of the whole region, never touching it.
Therefore x less than or equal to twelve is redundant. Its line never forms a boundary of the region, because the paper-and-quadrant constraints already do its job and more.
Removing it leaves the region unchanged, and therefore leaves the optimum of any linear objective over that region completely unchanged too.
The lesson is a useful habit. Not every line you are handed actually shapes the region. Before you solve, always check which constraints truly form the boundary and which are just along for the ride.

दोनों upper limits पर ध्यान दीजिए और first quadrant में इन्हें साथ मिलाकर सोचिए।

तो constraint x less than or equal to twelve असल में कभी bind कर ही नहीं सकती। बाकी constraints जो भी point allow करती हैं वो अपने आप x less than or equal to twelve को satisfy करता है, क्योंकि x पहले ही ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा दस है।
board इसे दिखाता है। line x equals twelve पूरे region के काफ़ी दाईं तरफ़ बैठती है, उसे कभी छूती नहीं।
इसलिए x less than or equal to twelve redundant है। इसकी line region की कोई boundary कभी नहीं बनाती, क्योंकि बाकी constraints पहले ही इसका काम, और उससे ज़्यादा, कर देती हैं।

सबक़ एक काम की आदत है। हर line जो आपको दी जाए वो असल में region को shape नहीं करती। solve करने से पहले, हमेशा check कीजिए कि कौन सी constraints सचमुच boundary बनाती हैं और कौन सी बस साथ आई हुई हैं।

sections.title: Special-case pitfalls and the five-second triage

board_events.text: Special-case pitfalls and a 5-second triage
Pitfall 1 — 'unbounded region' ⇒ 'no answer'. Wrong: most cost problems have a valid minimum.
Always run the half-plane test before declaring 'no optimum'.
Pitfall 2 — counting multiple optima as 'two'. A tie means infinitely many (the whole edge).
Pitfall 3 — missing infeasibility. If no common region exists, don't force corners — state it plainly.
Pitfall 4 — treating every constraint as binding. Some are redundant; check which form the boundary.
Triage: common region? (else infeasible) → bounded? (if yes both exist) → only if unbounded, verify.
This quick classification saves time and prevents every classic special-case error.

segments.text: Let me close the special cases with the four traps students fall into, and the quick triage that beats all of them.
Pitfall one, believing that an unbounded region means no answer. That is simply wrong. Most cost-minimisation problems have an unbounded region and a perfectly valid minimum.
So the rule is firm. Always run the half-plane test before you ever declare that there is no optimum.
Pitfall two, counting multiple optima as just two. A tie at two corners does not mean two answers. It means infinitely many, because the whole edge between them is optimal.
Pitfall three, missing infeasibility. If you cannot find a common shaded region, do not force yourself to invent corner points. State plainly that there is no feasible solution.
Pitfall four, treating every constraint as binding. Some constraints are redundant and never touch the region. Check which lines actually form the boundary before you solve.

And here is the triage that prevents all four. First, is there a common region? If not, it is infeasible. Second, is it bounded? If yes, both a max and a min exist and there is no special case. Only if it is unbounded do you need the verification test.
This five-second classification, done before you grind any numbers, saves time and prevents every one of the classic special-case errors.
special cases को उन चार traps से बंद करते हैं जिनमें students गिरते हैं, और उस quick triage से जो इन सबको हरा देती है।
pitfall one, यह मानना कि unbounded region का मतलब कोई answer नहीं। यह बिल्कुल ग़लत है। ज़्यादातर cost-minimisation problems में unbounded region और एक perfectly valid minimum होता है।
तो नियम पक्का है। कोई optimum नहीं, ऐसा declare करने से पहले हमेशा half-plane test चलाइए।
pitfall two, multiple optima को सिर्फ़ दो गिनना। दो corners पर tie का मतलब दो answers नहीं। इसका मतलब infinitely many, क्योंकि उनके बीच का पूरा edge optimal है।
pitfall three, infeasibility miss कर देना। अगर आपको common shaded region नहीं मिलता, तो खुद को corner points गढ़ने पर मजबूर मत कीजिए। साफ़ कहिए कि कोई feasible solution नहीं।
pitfall four, हर constraint को binding मानना। कुछ constraints redundant होती हैं और region को कभी छूती नहीं। solve करने से पहले check कीजिए कि कौन सी lines असल में boundary बनाती हैं।

और यह रही triage जो चारों को रोकती है। पहला, क्या common region है? अगर नहीं, तो infeasible। दूसरा, क्या bounded है? अगर हाँ, तो max और min दोनों exist करते हैं और कोई special case नहीं। सिर्फ़ अगर unbounded है, तब verification test चाहिए।
यह पाँच-second classification, numbers पीसने से पहले की गई, time बचाती है और हर classic special-case error रोकती है।

sections.title: Complete formula recap for the chapter

board_events.text: Formula recap — your complete Linear Programming toolkit
Standard maximisation (profit family):

board_events.latex: \text{Maximise } Z = ax + by \ \text{ s.t. } c_ix + d_iy \le e_i,\ \ x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0

board_events.text: Standard minimisation (cost family):

board_events.latex: \text{Minimise } Z = ax + by \ \text{ s.t. } c_ix + d_iy \ge e_i,\ \ x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0

board_events.text: Theorem 1: optimum at a corner. Theorem 2: bounded ⇒ both max & min; unbounded ⇒ may or may not.

board_events.latex: \text{no max if } ax + by \gt M \text{ meets } R; \qquad \text{no min if } ax + by \lt m \text{ meets } R

board_events.text: Trap translations: $-x + y \le k$ ('B exceeds A by at most $k$'); $x \ge 2y$ ('A at least twice B').

segments.text: Before the final revision card, here is your complete Linear Programming toolkit, gathered in one place. This section restates, it does not re-teach, so treat it as the sheet you glance at before the exam.
At the centre of everything is the objective function, Z equals a x plus b y.
First, the profit family, written as a maximisation.
Maximise Z equals a x plus b y, subject to each resource constraint c i x plus d i y less than or equal to e i, together with x and y greater than or equal to zero.
Second, the cost family, written as a minimisation.
Minimise Z equals a x plus b y, subject to each requirement c i x plus d i y greater than or equal to e i, again with x and y greater than or equal to zero.
Hold the two theorems firmly. Theorem one, the optimum sits at a corner. Theorem two, a bounded region guarantees both a maximum and a minimum, while an unbounded region may or may not have either.

And the two verification lines for unbounded regions. There is no maximum if a x plus b y greater than big M still meets the region, and no minimum if a x plus b y less than small m still meets the region.
Finally, keep the two trap translations at your fingertips. Minus x plus y less than or equal to k means B exceeds A by at most k, and x greater than or equal to two y means A is at least twice B.
आख़िरी revision card से पहले, यह रहा आपका पूरा Linear Programming toolkit, एक जगह इकट्ठा। यह section restate करता है, दोबारा नहीं पढ़ाता, तो इसे वो sheet समझिए जिसे आप exam से पहले एक नज़र देखते हैं।
हर चीज़ के केंद्र में है objective function, Z equals a x plus b y।
पहला, profit family, maximisation के रूप में।
Maximise Z equals a x plus b y, subject to हर resource constraint c i x plus d i y less than or equal to e i, साथ में x और y greater than or equal to zero।
दूसरा, cost family, minimisation के रूप में।
Minimise Z equals a x plus b y, subject to हर requirement c i x plus d i y greater than or equal to e i, फिर से x और y greater than or equal to zero।

दोनों theorems मज़बूती से पकड़िए। Theorem one, optimum किसी corner पर बैठता है। Theorem two, bounded region maximum और minimum दोनों guarantee करता है, जबकि unbounded region में इनमें से कोई हो भी सकता है और नहीं भी।

और unbounded regions के लिए दो verification lines। कोई maximum नहीं अगर a x plus b y greater than big M फिर भी region से मिलती है, और कोई minimum नहीं अगर a x plus b y less than small m फिर भी region से मिलती है।

आख़िर में, दोनों trap translations उँगलियों पर रखिए। minus x plus y less than or equal to k का मतलब B, A से ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा k बढ़ता है, और x greater than or equal to two y का मतलब A, B का कम से कम दोगुना है।

sections.title: One-screen chapter cheat sheet

board_events.text: Cheat sheet — one-screen revision
Objective $Z = ax + by$; constraints are linear inequalities plus non-negativity $x, y \ge 0$.
Corner-Point Method: draw region → list ALL vertices → tabulate $Z$ → pick best (verify if unbounded).
Bounded ⇒ both max & min exist. Unbounded ⇒ verify, or the optimum may vanish.
Translate words: 'at most / available' → ≤; 'at least / requires' → ≥; 'uses all / exactly' → =.
Four families: product-mix (max, ≤) · diet (min, ≥) · transport (≤ & ≥) · scheduling (time ≤, target ≥).
Four outcomes: unique · multiple (tie ⇒ whole edge) · unbounded solution · infeasible (empty region).
Memory aids: 'CORNERS not centres' · 'Most ≤, Least ≥' · 'Origin test' · 'region unbounded ≠ solution unbounded'.

segments.text: And finally, the one-screen cheat sheet. Everything in this chapter, compressed to what you can scan in the last minute before the paper.
The objective is always Z equals a x plus b y. The constraints are linear inequalities, plus the non-negativity conditions x and y greater than or equal to zero.
The engine is the corner-point method. Draw the region, list all vertices, tabulate Z at each, and pick the best, verifying if the region is unbounded.
The shape decides your safety. A bounded region guarantees both a maximum and a minimum. An unbounded region means you must verify, or the optimum may vanish.
Translate the words directly. At most or available becomes less-than-or-equal. At least or requires becomes greater-than-or-equal. Uses all or exactly becomes an equals sign.
Know the four families on sight. Product-mix is maximise with less-than-or-equal. Diet is minimise with greater-than-or-equal. Transport mixes both. Scheduling caps time and sets minimum targets.
And recognise the four outcomes. Unique optimum, multiple optima where a tie gives a whole edge, an unbounded solution with no finite optimum, and infeasible where the region is empty.

Carry the memory aids into the exam. Corners not centres. Most less-than-or-equal, least greater-than-or-equal. Use the origin test. And never forget, region unbounded is not the same as solution unbounded.
और आख़िर में, one-screen cheat sheet। इस chapter का सब कुछ, उतने में सिमटा जितना आप paper से एक minute पहले scan कर सकें।
objective हमेशा Z equals a x plus b y है। constraints linear inequalities हैं, साथ में non-negativity conditions x और y greater than or equal to zero।
engine है corner-point method। region draw कीजिए, सारे vertices list कीजिए, हर एक पर Z tabulate कीजिए, और best चुनिए, region unbounded हो तो verify करते हुए।
shape आपकी safety तय करती है। bounded region maximum और minimum दोनों guarantee करता है। unbounded region का मतलब आपको verify करना ही होगा, वरना optimum ग़ायब हो सकता है।
शब्दों को सीधे translate कीजिए। at most या available बनता है less-than-or-equal। at least या requires बनता है greater-than-or-equal। uses all या exactly बनता है equals sign।

चारों families देखते ही पहचानिए। product-mix है maximise with less-than-or-equal। diet है minimise with greater-than-or-equal। transport दोनों मिलाता है। scheduling time cap करता है और minimum targets रखता है।
और चारों outcomes पहचानिए। unique optimum, multiple optima जहाँ tie पूरा edge देता है, unbounded solution जिसमें कोई finite optimum नहीं, और infeasible जहाँ region खाली है।

memory aids exam में साथ ले जाइए। corners not centres। most less-than-or-equal, least greater-than-or-equal। origin test इस्तेमाल कीजिए। और कभी मत भूलिए, region unbounded, solution unbounded जैसा नहीं है।
